task.description: WF-02 Step 3 for REQ-134, implementing CODE-DESIGNER's approved design (gate-passed at step1b) as real, compilable test code. No lib/ module changes -- the design assigns all implementation to test-support/test code, so Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV) was skipped by the dispatching ORCH.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Implemented the design's full assertion contracts as real, compilable code: test/support/keycloak_test_client.ex (Letflow.Support.KeycloakTestClient, design S4.1's signatures exactly -- ensure_started/0, discovery_reachable?/1, direct_access_token/4, tamper_signature/1, the token_error() type, via Erlang's built-in :httpc/:inets, no new mix.exs dependency); test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs (Letflow.Integration.KeycloakAuthPipelineTest, @moduletag :keycloak, async: false, design S7.1's real-verifier setup/on_exit override, design S5's ensure_bpm_default_tenant!/0 get-or-create fixture inline in the test module per the design's own placement decision, and three test cases mapping to AC1/AC2/AC3 exactly as S7.2/S7.3/S7.4 specify); test/test_helper.exs changed to ExUnit.start(exclude: [:keycloak]) per design S2; test/specs/REQ-134.md written per the standard WF-02 Step 3 spec format.

mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force (MIX_ENV=test): PASSED CLEAN -- 'Compiling 131 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, zero errors.

AC4 default-exclusion, verified directly (Keycloak confirmed stopped via `docker compose ps` -- only the postgres service was Up): `mix test test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` -> 'Excluding tags: [:keycloak]' / 'All tests have been excluded.' / 'Result: 0 tests, 3 excluded'. A full default-suite run (all pre-existing tests) is TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 responsibility per the project's 'No Background Wait For A Cross-Turn Notification' rule -- a full mix test run is long-running and this run's own attempt at it exceeded the tool's synchronous timeout and was deliberately stopped (TaskStop) rather than left to notify a later turn that, as a dispatched subagent, would never arrive; the targeted-file exclusion evidence above is what this step's own instructions call for at minimum.

AC5, verified directly: `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` against stopped Keycloak produced 'RuntimeError) Keycloak not ready at http://localhost:8092/realms/bpm-default/.well-known/openid-configuration. Ensure docker-compose services are running (docker compose up -d keycloak) before executing these tests.' as the first and only surfaced reason, before any test in the module ran.

MINOR design/implementation discrepancy found and worked around, documented in the test module's own moduledoc and in test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC5 section: design S3.1 specifies setup_all returning {:skip, message}. Measured directly (elixir --version: Elixir 1.20.3 / ex_unit 1.20.3): this installed ExUnit version's setup_all callback does NOT accept {:skip, _} -- it raises a RuntimeError complaining the return shape is invalid, which is MORE obscure than a plain message (confirmed empirically: first attempt produced exactly this wrapped error). Also confirmed ExUnit's tag-based dynamic-skip path (ExUnit.Filters.eval/4) is evaluated from each test's compile-time tags map in runner.ex's prepare_tests/4, strictly before any setup_all/setup runs, so a runtime-computed skip reason cannot reach it either -- read ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/runner.ex and ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/filters.ex directly to confirm, not assumed. Adopted instead: setup_all raises a plain RuntimeError carrying the exact intended message text. ExUnit's own summary reports this as a failure ('all tests have been invalidated'), not literally 'skipped', but the message is exactly AC5's required two components (what's down, what to do) and is the first/only thing surfaced -- satisfies AC5's substance as closely as this toolchain allows. Not a silent resolution: flagged here per core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence 'never resolve a conflict silently' rule.

Keycloak reachability in this environment: NOT running (docker compose ps showed only the postgres service Up). AC1/AC2/AC3's live-Keycloak assertion output could not be captured by this step, as anticipated by the dispatching task -- that is TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 job (with Keycloak started) or an explicit environment-constraint note if Keycloak remains unavailable there too, matching REQ-128's precedent.

Developer command for AC6 (verified accurate against the actual file path and @moduletag): mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs

issues.description: design req134-real-keycloak-token-integration.md S3.1 specifies setup_all returning {:skip, message} to skip (not fail) the module when Keycloak is unreachable. This repo's installed ExUnit (1.20.3) does not support {:skip, _} as a setup_all return -- it raises a RuntimeError about the invalid return shape, which is MORE obscure than a plain targeted message, and ExUnit's tag-based dynamic-skip path runs before setup_all so it cannot substitute either. Worked around by raising a plain RuntimeError carrying the intended message text directly from setup_all -- ExUnit classifies this as a failure ('all tests have been invalidated'), not literally 'skipped', though the message itself satisfies AC5's substance. Documented in the test module's moduledoc and test/specs/REQ-134.md. Flagging for the design doc to be corrected at the source so a future reader does not re-derive this.
